title: Groundwater Sampling from Bores ~5 cm Wide and < 60 m Sampled Depth
author: Michael Lloyd Strack
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jvxcn7n
materials: Open the bore, remove any monitoring or logging equipment and record the time. This can help monitoring agencies to correct their data for any inaccurate readings.

steps.title: Record location and bore dimensions
steps.instruction: Record the GPS coordinates of the bore and note that the bore is approximately 5 cm wide and sampled to a depth of less than 60 m.

steps.title: Record monument or plaque information
steps.instruction: Write down any information that is displayed on the bore monument or plaque.

steps.title: Photograph bore and surroundings
steps.instruction: Take a photograph of the bore with its surrounding landscape visible in the background.

steps.title: Measure bore geometry with Aqua Dipper
steps.instruction: Using the Aqua Dipper Pro, (a) measure the distance from the mounting position to ground level, (b) measure the distance from the mounting position to the water table (if visible), and (c) measure the distance from the mounting position to the bottom of the bore hole.

steps.title: Remove dipper, record observations, store
steps.instruction: Remove the Aqua Dipper Pro, record any visual or olfactory observations about groundwater or sediment on the probe and tape, then store the dipper clean and dry.

steps.title: Inspect open bore hole visually and olfactorily
steps.instruction: Examine the open bore hole with a torch and your nose, recording any visual or olfactory observations while being careful of spiders, frogs, etc.

steps.title: Mount PowerPack PP1 on monument or ground
steps.instruction: Securely mount the PowerPack PP1 on the bore monument. If no monument is present, place the PP1 on the ground and stand firmly on the metal stand during pumping (hazardous).

steps.title: Determine target water‑bearing layer (optional)
steps.instruction: If you know the depth of a specific water‑bearing layer, use the Aqua Dipper Pro to measure the appropriate height on the sampling hose (starting from the foot‑valve), add extra height for the monument if present, and mark the hose. Place the foot‑valve approximately 20 cm below the layer’s lower bound (unless the layer is artesian). Note that this method is imperfect; use well packers for accurate isolation.

steps.title: Insert and position sampling hose
steps.instruction: Insert the sampling hose (foot‑valve end first) down the bore‑hole while swabbing the exterior with bleach on a cloth. If the bore is uncased, jiggle and rotate as needed. • If targeting a specific layer, clamp the hose to the PowerPack PP1 when the marked height is level with the bore opening. • If not targeting, lower the hose until the foot‑valve contacts the bottom, then pull it up about 1 m to lift it above settled sediment before clamping. Watch for small stones that may wedge the valve open; if pumping is ineffective, draw the hose out to check. Use a hose long enough to avoid dropping it irretrievably; be prepared for heavy, water‑filled hose in deep bores.

steps.title: Mount Aqua Dipper Pro for later measurements
steps.instruction: Re‑mount the Aqua Dipper Pro on the bore (for later depth‑to‑water‑table measurement).

steps.title: Assemble flow cell apparatus and power meters
steps.instruction: Assemble the flow‑cell apparatus with its probes and turn on the calibrated, tested, and fully charged water meters.

steps.title: Connect flow cell to splitter and set valves
steps.instruction: Attach the flow‑cell apparatus to one outlet of the flow splitter (the “flow‑cell outlet”). Turn the flow‑cell outlet valve to CLOSED and the other outlet (“open outlet”) to OPEN. Place the flow cell and its inflow tubing in the shade to minimise solar UV/IR effects; outflow tubing exposure is not a concern.

steps.title: Arrange purge containers within outlet range
steps.instruction: Position purge storage containers so they are reachable from both the open outlet of the flow splitter and the flow‑cell outlet tubing, allowing you to redirect outflow without moving the flow‑cell apparatus.

steps.title: Double‑check setup and secure hose
steps.instruction: Verify that all equipment is prepared and secured. Because the sampling hose will shift and coils will tighten during pumping, arrange the bulk of the hose away from the flow cell and other gear before starting.

steps.title: Start PowerPack PP1 on low throttle
steps.instruction: Record the start time and start the PowerPack PP1 motor on low throttle. Ensure the fuel tank is topped up before starting (better to refuel beforehand than to interrupt sampling).

steps.title: Position hose end toward purge container
steps.instruction: Firmly grasp the end of the sampling hose just before the flow splitter and point the open outlet toward the purge container.

steps.title: Increase throttle to initiate flow
steps.instruction: If needed, increase the PowerPack PP1 throttle until groundwater begins to exit the open outlet into the purge container. The hose will twitch, jerk, and tighten; maintain a steady hand.

steps.title: Observe efflux and adjust flow rate
steps.instruction: Watch the efflux: clear water followed by turbid water that slowly clears. Keep flow rate low enough to avoid bursting flow‑splitter or flow‑cell fittings and to prevent excessive drawdown that could collapse an uncased bore.

steps.title: Open flow‑cell valve and stabilize flow
steps.instruction: When you judge that the groundwater will not clog the flow cells, direct the flow‑cell outlet tubing into the purge container and gently open the flow‑cell valve on the splitter until a steady flow passes through the flow‑cell apparatus. If fittings begin to burst, reduce throttle, close the flow‑cell valve slightly, and tape fittings firmly with duct tape.

steps.title: Take initial water‑meter readings and volume
steps.instruction: Record the first water‑meter readings (pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, temperature) and note the volume of groundwater purged. If working alone, briefly stop pumping to take the readings. To avoid air bubbles, orient the flow‑splitter so the open outlet is uppermost and the flow‑cell outlet is underneath.

steps.title: Purge to half of intended volume
steps.instruction: Continue pumping and taking water‑meter readings until approximately half of the intended purge volume has been removed.

steps.title: Purge to full intended volume
steps.instruction: Continue pumping and taking readings until the full intended purge volume has been removed.

steps.title: Check reading stability and continue if needed
steps.instruction: If the last two consecutive readings differ by more than about 10 %, keep purging in the same volume increments until the readings stabilise. If they never stabilise, you may stop purging and collect the sample, but note that the sample may not be representative of a single aquifer.

steps.title: Collect and seal groundwater sample
steps.instruction: Pump water into a cleaned, sterilised sample container, rinse and discard this first water, then fill the container to overflowing (to exclude air) and seal it tightly.

steps.title: Label sample and store in cooler
steps.instruction: Write the sample ID on the container and place it in a portable cooler on ice, kept in the dark.

steps.title: Record pump stop time
steps.instruction: Record the time when pumping ceased.

steps.title: Clean and pack flow‑cell probes
steps.instruction: Remove the probes from the flow cells, rinse them with MilliQ water, dry them, and pack them away.

steps.title: Unclamp and withdraw sampling hose
steps.instruction: Unclamp the sampling hose from the PowerPack PP1 and pull it out of the bore hole.

steps.title: Drain remaining water from hose
steps.instruction: Lift the foot‑valve end of the hose so groundwater flows away, then walk along the hose, lifting it as you go, until most water has exited.

steps.title: Bleach hose interior and pack away
steps.instruction: Pour approximately 250 mL of bleach into the foot valve and walk the bleach along the hose and out the outlets; then pack the hose away.

steps.title: Remove, refuel, and pack PowerPack
steps.instruction: Remove the PowerPack PP1, top up its fuel tank, and pack the unit away.

steps.title: Detach and clean flow‑cell apparatus
steps.instruction: Detach the flow‑cell apparatus from the flow splitter, rinse it with MilliQ water, dry it, and pack it away.

steps.title: Measure water‑table depth and calculate drawdown
steps.instruction: Use the Aqua Dipper Pro to measure the depth to the water table and calculate the drawdown.

steps.title: Replace logging instruments and record time
steps.instruction: Replace any logging instruments that were removed and record the time of replacement.

steps.title: Close bore lid and replace padlock
steps.instruction: Close the bore lid and, if present, replace the padlock.
